correctness.rationale: Ideal intersections in Z/(p^alpha q^beta) are controlled by coordinatewise maxima, giving the exact decomposition K_(alpha beta-1) join (K_alpha union K_beta). The three canonical parts are true-twin classes, which proves that no forcing set can omit two vertices from one part and that one omitted vertex in each of all three parts stalls. Every cross-part white pair forces, so the polynomial has exactly the three claimed terms. The real Gram witness with vectors (1,0), (0,1), and (1,1) has rank two and exactly the graph pattern. The recognizability proof reduces equal polynomials to either equal exponent sum/product or the involutive equations s'=t-2, t'=s+2; elementary inequalities and factorization of 6 leave exactly the two stated collisions.

value.rationale: The finding gives the entire zero forcing polynomial, all minimum forcing sets, and an exact recognizability theorem on a classical family of ring intersection graphs. The identification of exactly two nonisomorphic polynomial collisions is a natural and nonroutine classification result that goes beyond the previously known zero forcing number.
